sources.title: P. Etingof, S. Gelaki, D. Nikshych, and V. Ostrik, Tensor Categories (MIT 18.769 full course lecture notes, 2009)
sources.locator: Complete 128-page notes; focused §1.10 (PDF pp. 26–29), §1.21 (PDF pp. 43–45), and §1.35 ordinary Hopf specialization (PDF pp. 71–72).

contents.name: Definitions 1.10.1–1.10.2: the two dual orientations, evaluations, coevaluations, and triangle identities
contents.reason: The page states both evaluation and coevaluation orientations explicitly and proves the module-map and triangle identities under its declared finite-dimensional hypothesis.

contents.name: Example 1.10.12: finite-dimensional vector spaces are rigid; arbitrary vector spaces need not be
contents.reason: The local proof constructs coevaluation from a finite dual basis and records why the algebraic finite-dimensional hypothesis cannot be dropped.

contents.name: Example 1.10.13: contragredient dual of a finite-dimensional group representation
contents.reason: The worked C2 module computes the inverse-action formula, invariant evaluation, invariant coevaluation, and the triangle composites.

contents.name: Definition 1.21.2 and the Rep(H) construction: bialgebra modules tensor by Δ with unit action ε
contents.reason: The carrier constructs the tensor action and unit explicitly, proves their module and naturality properties, and checks the constraints on elements.

contents.name: Theorem 1.21.3: reconstruction of a finite bialgebra from a tensor category and fiber functor
contents.reason: This reconstruction classification is outside the page's direct construction and regular-module converse; no reconstruction theorem is claimed.

contents.name: §1.35 ordinary Hopf specialization: the dual module action via S and H-linearity of evaluation and coevaluation
contents.reason: The ordinary Hopf case is checked locally from the two antipode identities; the quasi-Hopf correction elements are not imported.

sources.title: Christoph Schweigert, Hopf algebras, quantum groups and topological field theory (Hamburg University full lecture notes, version dated 31 October 2025)
sources.locator: Complete 219-page notes; focused Observation 2.3.2 (PDF p. 22), §§2.6–2.7.16 (PDF pp. 34–60), and §5.1 (PDF pp. 159–160).

contents.name: Observation 2.3.2: group-algebra tensor action and contragredient dual action
contents.reason: The example checks these formulas concretely for C2 and identifies the S-action with the inverse group element.

contents.name: §2.6: tensor products of bialgebra modules and the associator and unit constraints
contents.reason: The local theorem proves Δ multiplicativity and counitality give H-linear constraints and derives the converse from regular modules.

contents.name: Lemma 2.7.8: inverse-antipode cancellation identities when S is bijective
contents.reason: The local right-dual proof derives both reversed cancellation identities from the ordinary antipode equations and bijectivity.

contents.name: Proposition 2.7.11: Hom-space actions and dual actions via S and S inverse
contents.reason: The page defines both linear dual actions and proves the action maps are algebra representations under the corresponding antipode hypotheses.

contents.name: Definition 2.7.12 and Lemma 2.7.13: dual-object triangle axioms and finite dimensionality of vector-space dualizable objects
contents.reason: The local carrier proves both triangle composites from a finite dual basis and excludes the unsupported infinite-dimensional coevaluation claim.

contents.name: Proposition 2.7.16 and Corollary 2.7.17: H-linearity of evaluations and coevaluations and rigidity of finite-dimensional Hopf modules with inverse antipode
contents.reason: The local proofs expand the same antipode cancellations and preserve separate hypotheses for the S and S inverse orientations.

contents.name: Definition 5.1.1 and Proposition 5.1.3: group-like pivots with S squared equal to conjugation
contents.reason: The local formula j_p(v)=j(pv) is checked for H-linearity and natural monoidal behavior under the group-like pivot hypothesis.
